candidate: raise the two-phase decode split's slice cap from 4 to 16, for both head geometries, and retire the 512-keys-per-slice doubling rule (hipengine/kernels/hip_gfx1100/gemma4/gemma4_attention.py)
reason: the 4-slice cap was asserted rather than measured. The policy's own docstring said more slices is better until the cap and never justified the cap; measured properly, 4 was far too few at every point tested, and 16 is optimal or within 4% everywhere. The cap was wrong by 4x, not by a margin.

mechanism.structure: unchanged from the accepted two-phase split: phase 1 writes pass 2's weights and denominator, phase 2 accumulates a slice's weighted-V sum, a combine sums the slices in ascending order and divides by phase 1's denominator. Only the number of slices changes, so the only arithmetic change is the association order of the same f32 sum over more partials.

per_launch_ab.method: paired interleaved arms, one pass per arm per run, two runs per arm, both GPUs idle, monkeypatching decode_slices; us per launch on GPU1
per_launch_ab.policy_choice: 16 is optimal or within 4% at every point but full/8192, where 32 is 8% better. The per-geometry refinement is deliberately not taken: a microbenchmark establishes a direction, not an end-to-end win, and iteration 35 was reverted for exactly that over-extrapolation. One number is one thing to justify.
per_launch_ab.retired_rule: the doubling rule kept more than 512 keys per slice and returned 2 slices at exactly 1024 keys. The table shows 64 keys per slice to be the fastest configuration measured, so the floor it encoded was simply wrong. decode_slices no longer takes head_dim, since nothing above the entry threshold depends on it.

correctness.gate: NOT COVERED - see gate_gap. The teacher-forced evaluator was run and reports kl_max 0.0 exactly with zero top-1 flips over all 1023 rows, but that is bit-identity of the single-kernel path against itself, not evidence about the split.

gate_gap.finding: the teacher-forced gate never exercises the decode split, and did not before this change either.
gate_gap.mechanism: scripts/gemma4_teacher_forced_gate.py capture_chain feeds the prompt one token at a time from an empty cache (runner.forward([ids[position]])), so key counts run 1, 2, 3, ... 1023 - one token below the split's 1024-key entry threshold. decode_slices returns 1 for every row.
gate_gap.evidence: instrumented run: decode_slices called 30 times per forward (once per layer) with keys=[1] at position 0, [2] at position 1, ... [5] at position 4; slices=1 at every one. After a 600-token prefill the same instrumentation reports keys=601, 602, 603, 604, so prefill-then-decode does engage the split.
gate_gap.consequence: the 2026-09-25 split gate result (kl_max 0.0067, recorded in the two-phase-split acceptance) measured the sliding read range, not the split. That claim is corrected here rather than left standing.
gate_gap.fix_owed: prefill the chain and re-capture the baseline at >= 1024 keys, then re-gate the split. This changes the frozen evaluator and its baseline artifact, so it is owed as its own unit rather than folded into this one.

correctness.parity: tests/test_gpu_gemma4_attention_decode_parity.py passes at 16 slices (it calls decode_slices, so the slice count changed with the policy): f32 within 1e-4 and bf16 within one bf16 ulp on the artifact's two real geometries at 1024, 2055 and 8192 keys
correctness.token_parity: 128 greedy positions at a 1024-token prompt produce identical token ids at 4 and 16 slices (0 differing positions), measured through the runner's forward path rather than inferred from the row
correctness.red_first: the routing unit test pinned the old policy (4 at 1024 keys, 2 for the wide geometry) and failed on the change, which is what identified the wide-geometry rule as also wrong rather than only the narrow-head cap

performance.label: split-16-slices

campaign_rows.regression_check: no row regressed. The 128p and 512p rows are below the 1024-key entry threshold, so they take the single-kernel path with byte-identical arguments and are untouched by construction, not merely unregressed. Prefill is untouched by construction (the split applies only at tokens == 1).
campaign_rows.caveat: the primary row is a median of 3 samples; the other rows are 2 samples each, measured in the same session as the change. Both flat rows are below the split threshold, so their deltas are noise by construction rather than a measurement of the change.

performance.campaign_position: 45.8427 -> 48.2630 tok/s at 1024p/128o, 3.0x the 16.0931 baseline and 60.2% of the campaign's 70%-of-Qwen stop condition
performance.interpretation: the win is larger at 4096p than at the metric row because the split's benefit scales with keys per slice while its fixed cost does not: the sliding layers walk 1024 keys at both rows (the read range caps them at the window), but the 5 full layers walk ~1152 keys at the metric row against ~4224 at 4096p, and full/8192 is where the table shows the largest gain.

scope.flags_added: none. The slice count is a policy constant with the measured table in its docstring.
scope.fallbacks: none: below 1024 keys the launcher takes the single-kernel path by policy, which is a measured choice with a named threshold, not a fallback from a failed path.
